title: AMIE: conversational diagnostic AI rated above primary care physicians in simulated consultations
summary: In a blinded remote OSCE with 149 case scenarios, AMIE and primary care physicians held text consultations with simulated patients. Specialist physicians rated AMIE superior on 30 of 32 axes and patient actors on 25 of 26, and non-inferior on the rest. The evidence comes from simulated scenarios, not real patients, and the authors state that further research is needed before real-world use.
ai_technology: AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), a large language model agent for diagnostic dialogue

evidence.tested: A randomized, double-blind crossover study of text consultations with patient-actors across 159 case scenarios compared AMIE with 20 primary care physicians, rated by specialist physicians and patient actors on several axes.
evidence.unknown: The authors note the unfamiliar synchronous text-chat format and state that further research is needed before real-world use.
evidence.ai_role: AMIE, an LLM-based diagnostic dialogue system trained by self-play with automated feedback, conducted the consultations.
